package.author: Jean-Pierre Bergamin
package.description: Command-line emulator of classic HP calculators

en-US.author: Jean-Pierre Bergamin
en-US.description: Command-line emulator of classic HP calculators
en-US.longDescription: saturnus emulates the HP 48SX, 48GX, 49G, 38G, 39G, 40G, 42S, 27S, 17BII, 17B, 28S and 19BII from their own ROMs. The command line runs a calculator without a window: it presses keys listed in a text file, saves the screen as text or a PNG, serves the serial port and looks up the built-in commands. No ROM is included.
en-US.name: saturnus (command line)
en-US.releaseNotes:
Download the desktop app
- Mac (Apple silicon): saturnus_0.11.0_aarch64.dmg
- Windows (Intel or AMD): saturnus_0.11.0_x64-setup.exe
- Windows on ARM: saturnus_0.11.0_arm64-setup.exe
The Windows installers are not signed yet: if Windows says "Windows protected your PC", click "More info", then "Run anyway".
Linux, the .msi installers, the command-line tools and satx: see Assets at the end of this page.
saturnus 0.11.0 brings an HP 100LX or 200LX palmtop into Files, lets Files
use the 49G's XSERV, makes Files simpler, and offers the calculators to
your browser's own AI (WebMCP).

Get it
- On the web, nothing to install: https://ractive.ch/saturnus/app/
  (Chrome, Edge or Firefox for a serial cable; every browser for the
  emulated calculator).
- The desktop app saturnus_0.11.0_… (on Linux saturnus-app), with
  a -SHA256SUMS file beside them:
  - macOS, Apple silicon: .dmg, signed and notarised, or brew trust --cask ractive/tap/saturnus-app once, then brew install --cask ractive/tap/saturnus-app;
  - Windows: .msi or -setup.exe for x86_64 (x64) and ARM (arm64);
  - Linux: .deb, .rpm or .AppImage for x86_64 (amd64, x86_64)
    and ARM (arm64, aarch64). Add yourself to the dialout group to
    use a serial port.
- The command-line tools saturnus and satx: cargo install,
  Homebrew ractive/tap, Scoop ractive, or the archives and Linux
  packages below.
- Libraries on crates.io, all at 0.11.0, among them the new
  filer-proto.

Files
- An HP 100LX or 200LX palmtop. "Add a calculator…" offers "An HP
  100LX or 200LX palmtop": put its Filer in server mode, and Files shows
  its drives, folders and files, copies both ways (whole folders too),
  renames, deletes and makes folders. 19200 baud by default. Use the
  palmtop's own cable, never on a 48 or 49G.
- XSERV on the 49G. Type XSERV on the 49G instead of SERVER, and
  Files finds it by itself: about twice as fast as the Kermit server,
  and the list does not depend on the display. For PICT, backup and
  restore Files starts the Kermit server inside XSERV and comes back.
- One connect step. Files reads the model from the calculator: the
  connect step shows each model's keys, and the model picker and the
  Settings dialog are gone ("Use a fixed speed" is under "Trouble with
  the cable?").
- A calculator that stops answering says so, after 25 seconds on the
  Kermit server or 8 on XSERV, with the keys to start it again and
  Reconnect.
- Fast transfer by one key on the 48GX (and a 49G without XSERV):
  Files puts the command on the calculator's stack, and you press EVAL.
- A 38G, 39G or 40G sees new files at once, without serving again.

Your AI
- The browser's own AI (WebMCP). In a browser with WebMCP (Chrome 149
  and Edge 150 try it out on saturnus's site), the calculators' tools are
  offered to the browser's AI as well, with no address or code. The app
  adds no question of its own; the browser or its AI decides whether to
  ask you before storing or purging a variable (Brave's Leo asks before
  every call). Connecting an AI app through the dialog works as before.
- A cancelled AI call stops at once and leaves no keys behind.

satx
- satx lx: files on an HP 100LX or 200LX over its Filer.
- XSERV: satx info says which server answered; satx xserv was
  tested on a real 49G.
- A real 49G read whole. The 49G sends each stack level only as wide
  as its display, so satx info failed on a 49G with ROM 1.18; IOPAR and
  the version are now read in pieces, in any display mode.

Smaller changes
- The home page says "Add an emulated calculator" and "Connect a real
  calculator".
- The reference gives the 49G's EVAL key (right-shift, SYMB); the
  Reference tab names search's key.
- Pressed buttons keep their look under the pointer.
- Disconnect lets go of the serial port within 30 seconds.
